headline: South Asia: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week.
- Africa: Ethiopia: Lethal Artillery Strikes On Civilian Neighbourhoods in Tigray's Alamata City Must Be Investigated As War Crimes.
- Korean Peninsula: Ukraine attacks Russian freighter accused of smuggling North Korean arms in past.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
- Military Times, one day ago: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
Trump said he wanted to move forward with the controlled blasts but is putting the decision in the hands of the courts.
- Military Times, one day ago: B-2 bomber wings awarded Presidential Unit Citation for Midnight Hammer.
The award marks the first time a bomber unit has been recognized with a President Unit Citation since the Vietnam War.
- Military Times, one day ago: Under Hegseth, the OSS rides again — kind of.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth resurrected the OSS, created during the Second World War under "Wild Bill" Donovan.
- Military Times, one day ago: VFW seeks veterans’ input on health care experiences in and out of VA.
Through early January, Veterans of Foreign Wars is conducting a survey of veterans on their health care experiences, including medical treatment received at the Department of Veterans Affairs or in private care.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 19 hours ago: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
Local and international partners could become reluctant to donate to Jamaica in future national emergencies if confidence in the management of humanitarian aid is not urgently restored, Opposition Spokesperson on Local Government Natalie Neita Garvey has warned. This comes amid findings from a report by the auditor general that the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) misused funds donated for a Government-directed roof programme to clear third-party goods.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 19 hours ago: Wright: They behave like hooligans but want to be called honourable.
WESTERN BUREAU: Amid deepening political rifts that have spilled from Gordon House into the courts, outspoken educator Linvern Wright is accusing some parliamentarians of abandoning principles, fairness and national responsibility in favour of partisan warfare.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 6 hours ago: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
Despite September's month-over-month growth, poor figures for July and August dragged down quarterly performance. Economists are already warning of “stagflation” La entrada Argentina officially enters a technical recession se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian drone strikes civilian car in Sumy: 76-year-old man killed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Russian drone strikes civilian car in Sumy: 76-year-old man killed.
A Russian fibre-optic FPV drone hit a civilian car in Sumy's Kovpakivskyi district, killing a 76-year-old passenger; his son, the driver, is in hospital.
- The Moscow Times, 10 hours ago: Zelensky Confirms Ukraine Was Behind Drone Attack on Russian Cargo Ship in Gulf of Finland.
Volodymyr Zelensky said the cargo ship Sparta II and "every vessel with a Russian flag" are legitimate targets for Ukrainian strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Ukrainian foreign minister advises Putin to stop complaining about strikes on oil refineries and end war instead.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has responded to Russian ruler Vladimir Putin's complaints about Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, advising him to order an end to the war instead.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Number of Russian attacks on Naftogaz facilities since start of war exceeds 800.
Naftogaz says its facilities have been struck more than 800 times since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, but its plants continue producing oil and gas.
Southern Europe - bottom line: MI5 warns UK defense firms they are target of Russian attacks.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: MI5 warns UK defense firms they are target of Russian attacks.
An increased threat of Russian attacks across Europe has prompted British intelligence to call on U.K. defense firms to take action to protect themselves.
- Balkan Insight, 8 hours ago: Belgrade Court Convicts Bosnian Serb Woman of Wartime Killings.
The Higher Court in Belgrade found Visnja Acimovic guilty of involvement in the murder of at least 30 Bosniak civilians in June 1992 in the Vlasenica area during the Bosnian war.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: COP must change after Antalya failure, UK climate chief warns.
Rachel Kyte said it was time to “blow the whistle” on COP’s failings.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: Wildberger reagiert skeptisch auf Weimers TikTok-Vorstoß.
Der Digitalminister dämpft die Erwartungen an einen europäischen TikTok-Deal. Ein Verkauf allein reiche nicht – auch die Technologie dahinter müsse nach Europa kommen.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 19 hours ago: Nigeria: Military Air Interdictions Eliminate 37 Terrorists, Destroy Logistics Assets in North-East.
[This Day] Abuja -- The sustained operational pressure exerted by air assets of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), on terrorist elements through a series of intelligence-led precision air strikes across the theatre has resulted in the killing of 37 terrorists and the destruction of their logistics assets, the Nigerian military has said.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Namibia: Namibia Urges Stronger Enforcement of Child Marriage Laws.
[New Era] Namibian parliamentarian Nelson Kalangula has called for stronger implementation and greater public awareness of laws aimed at eradicating child marriage, saying legislation alone is insufficient without the understanding and support of political, traditional and community leaders.

[New Era] Namibia is seeking to move beyond exporting uranium and start adding more value to the mineral locally as the government looks to expand the nuclear industry's contribution to the economy.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week.
Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”. The building, which was also attacked last Thursday, is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Houthis restarted in July. Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported Tuesday’s injuries and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 7 hours ago: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 7, including senior security official.
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials in the territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire in place since last year. Israel’s military said it had struck a senior Hamas official. Gaza’s interior ministry said an airstrike in Gaza City killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahal, director-general of the Internal Security Service. Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, told AFP that several other people were in critical condition following the same strike in Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Balochistan govt announces rewards of up to Rs250m for information on wanted terrorists.
QUETTA: The Balochistan government has announced rewards ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs250 million for providing authentic information about most-wanted terrorists in the province. According to an official advertisement issued by the provincial government, a reward of Rs250m has been fixed for information about Bashir Zeb of the banned Balochistan Liberation Army and Abdul Rehman alias Rehman Gul. Similar rewards have been fixed for other wanted persons depending on their status.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday awarded the Medal of Freedom, the country’s highest civilian honour, to Rudy Giuliani, the former New York mayor who became a national figure after the September 11, 2001, attacks and later helped Trump try to overturn his 2020 election defeat. - Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row.
Concerns are mounting among political leaders, notably PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, regarding the construction activities near Sheshnag Lake. Environmental advocates and Congress members underscore the area's ecological sensitivity. The Border Roads Organisation defends its initiatives as critical for ensuring safety for pilgrims on the Amarnath Yatra route. MacKenzie Scott has donated $62 million to the marine conservation organization Blue Ventures for their 2030 goals. This donation will support small-scale fishing communities and their efforts in marine ecosystem conservation. The funding aims to enhance local stewardship of carbon-rich seas and improve food security in coastal areas. Blue Ventures will allocate funds through the Frontline Community Fund to empower local partners effectively.

Gukesh drew his opening 38-move World Championship game against Javokhir Sindarov despite facing severe time pressure and an aggressive opening attack. Playing with black, he showed excellent defensive skills, neutralised Sindarov’s advantage and escaped danger without major mistakes. Although the match ended level, Gukesh gained a psychological victory, boosting his confidence ahead of Game 2.
